reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that modern sports science tools excel at generating numerical outputs but fail to communicate the epistemic uncertainty inherent in those estimates. This leads to misinterpretation of thresholds and overconfidence in deterministic conclusions. The honesty layer addresses this by embedding calibrated uncertainty into decision-making processes. It operates through a dual mechanism: first, it applies conformal prediction techniques to quantify how wrong a given score might be; second, it introduces a selective-gate mechanism that allows for abstention when uncertainty exceeds predefined bounds. These primitives form a coherent mathematical structure where each component contributes to a robust, uncertainty-aware decision framework. The failure mode arises when vendors treat all outputs as definitive, ignoring the probabilistic nature of underlying data. In contrast, the proposed honesty layer ensures that decisions are made only when sufficient evidence supports them, thereby reducing false positives and improving operational reliability.
